strengths: First volumetric functional maps framework addressing an open problem; mathematically principled extension of surface methods with proper LBO discretization and boundary condition handling
Comprehensive experimental validation across 40-pair ground truth set and multiple benchmark datasets (SHREC'19/20, TOPKIDS) with multiple bases (LBO, CMH, Orthoprods)

Multiple practical contributions demonstrated: spectral connectivity transfer methods, volume-aware surface correspondence (60-68% success on SHREC'20 vs 22-60% surface-only), and dramatic mesh untangling improvement (85% on 1405 previously failed cases)
Rigorous theoretical appendices (B-D) analyzing spectral consistency, isometry preservation between volumetric and surface representations, and boundary trace expressiveness
Seamless integration with existing functional map extensions (CMH, Orthoprods) and algorithmic details enabling reproducibility; code release promised
weaknesses: Limited volumetric dataset availability: validation heavily dependent on tetrahedralizations of surface benchmarks, which introduces topological noise and artifacts (acknowledged limitation in Section 5.4); tetrahedralization itself degrades spectral properties, requiring CMH regularization to compensate

Significant computational overhead (1.01-2.51× slowdown for surface matching) with no consistent practical benefit; full bijectivity in connectivity transfer requires prohibitively expensive 25% of spectrum; MATLAB implementation not production-ready

Connectivity transfer remains incomplete: never achieves bijective maps without external mesh untangling; at 20% spectrum still retains 0.34-0.42% flipped cells (Table 1); acknowledged as 'far from being perfect'

Inconsistent and basis-dependent shape matching results: improvements limited to specific datasets/bases (e.g., VOL dataset benefits only from Orthoprods); SHREC'20 performance reversal when switching from LBO to CMH suggests volumetric signal diluted by numerical artifacts; raises unresolved question of when volumetric information actually helps

Missing fundamental theoretical analysis: authors explicitly state this remains future work; no formal characterization of invariant properties under volumetric maps or principled guidance for basis selection; spectral stability in discrete setting uncharacterized

Insufficient medical validation: single brain segmentation example without quantitative metrics; no comparison with established registration methods (LDDMM, demons) despite medical motivation; limited evidence of clinical utility

Basis selection lacks principled guidance: choice among LBO/CMH/Orthoprods is dataset-dependent; CMH works better but mixes extrinsic information, undermining pure volumetric approach; hyperparameter tuning required per dataset (Appendix H)
